pr_metadata.title: feat(box): box gc --unreferenced reclaims boxes no catalog selection resolves to
pr_metadata.summary: Adds an opt-in mqlab box gc --unreferenced pass that deregisters, deletes the caches of, and reclaims the base volumes of boxes no current catalog selection can resolve to on any host (e.g. infra/obs/san-ubuntu24 after infra moved to ubuntu:26), never touching a resolvable box or one a live VM backs onto.
pr_metadata.notes:
Protected set: box.resolvable_box_names = Catalog.all_boxes(None, stack_roles) (new facts=None means no host filter: every SUPPORTED OS of every stack plus the shared roles on infra/infra_mq) + every catalog OS base box + this host's FLEET. Deliberately not host-filtered because build/state/boxes is persistent (RHEL 10 on a non-v3 host stays protected). Candidates are only generated <role>-<os><major> names found registered, cached as <box>-<arch>.box/.manifest-hash/.components.json (any arch), or holding pool volumes; base boxes, cloud images and foreign names are reported as kept and never touched; retired names stay with the retired pass. A candidate whose base image backs a live overlay is kept and reported. Removed boxes' volumes go via gc_orphaned_images(dead_stems=...), keeping none (in-use guard still holds). Report prints the commands run (vagrant box remove, rm) plus every kept box and why. Opt-in flag; plain box gc unchanged; --dry-run previews. Pool absent (#1415) is tolerated (no VM disks to protect); any other virsh failure aborts before removing anything. Docs: docs/development/box-model.md. REMAINING ACCEPTANCE (human, after merge): run mqlab box gc --unreferenced --dry-run, then mqlab box gc --unreferenced, on both hosts; not run against real host boxes here.
